raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Native generation reads `sampling_params["n"]` before constructing `SamplingParams`. Explicit `null` therefore raises a `TypeError` during request normalization even though `SamplingParams` treats it as the default of 1. Zero, negative, boolean and non-integer values can also reach request expansion without a consistent validation error.

Related prior work: #28858 (closed by its author, not merged). This PR independently focuses only on sample-count normalization and validation; it does not change stop-string or regex handling.

## Modifications

- Share a small `normalize_sample_count` helper between `SamplingParams` construction and native request normalization.
- Treat omitted/null `n` as 1 and reject other values unless they are positive integers, before request expansion and beam-search fan-out handling.
- Cover single/batched inputs, dict/list sampling parameters, invalid counts, and valid beam requests without fan-out. Existing valid parallel-sampling tests remain unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU-only validation on Python 3.12. No server, GPU or model weights used.

- Both registered test files execute successfully through their native unittest entrypoints: 80 sampling tests and 68 IO-struct tests (2 skipped).
- New focused regression checks fail against the unchanged production files from base `20036b7add8c573cf74364028d13a3ec18bdd3c6` and pass with this patch.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` pass. Repository-wide pre-commit has not been run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. This changes request-boundary validation only and makes no inference-performance claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Run applicable pre-commit hooks on changed files.
- [x] Add focused regression tests to existing registered test files.
- [ ] Run repository-wide pre-commit.
- [ ] Upstream CI and maintainer review.

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and testing. Draft pending upstream validation.

+    """Resolve the default and validate n before parallel request expansion."""

+        raise ValueError(f"n must be a positive integer, got {n!r}.")
